channel.title: The Brilliant Employee
channel.description: One person, one AI employee, and the workplace built around him so the work can be trusted.

item.title: The Loop That Would Learn Backwards
item.description: A learning loop is not proven by the fact that it learns. It is proven by the direction. Mine had the sign the wrong way round.

item.title: The Lethal Trifecta
item.description: Reading untrusted pages, sending messages, and holding private files are each safe alone. Together they are an exfiltration pipe.

item.title: The Ledger: one line per task, forever
item.description: Every finished task appends a line to a file the model never writes to itself. Without it, an improvement claim is a memory of feeling faster.

item.title: The Scorekeeper With an Eraser
item.description: My scoreboard read 79.3%. A prior in the reporting script was discarding one model's successes before the arithmetic ran.

item.title: Failure Arrives in the Same Tone as Success
item.description: Sixteen nightly backups were dead and nothing reported it, because a job that does nothing and a job that works print the same quiet output.

item.title: Worse Than a Coin Flip
item.description: I ran my router against a benchmark I did not write. It scored worse than choosing at random, and I published the number.

item.title: The Homework That Was Impossible
item.description: A queue reported nothing waiting, which is the same string a healthy queue prints. Two correct components had starved the pool to nothing.

item.title: My gate recommends the cheap model 89% of the time. It ran 0.2% of the time.
item.description: My triage step sizes nine tasks in ten to the cheapest model. I quoted that for five weeks as what my system did. It is not.

item.title: The Leak Was in the AI's Own Chat Logs
item.description: My audit agent reported leaked tokens at a named path. The path had never existed. Dismissing it there would have been the mistake.

item.title: The employee I never interviewed
item.description: You cannot vet an AI worker the way you vet a person. So I stopped trying, and built the workplace around him instead.
